findings.title: Codex response filename is not bound to jq's input operand
findings.observation: Cycle 7 binds predicates to one parsed shell segment, but the SINGULAR branch only checks arguments_.includes(responseFile). It never identifies which positional jq operand is the input JSON file.
findings.trigger: Use one jq command: jq --arg marker replay-response.json '{requestId: .meta.requestId}' unrelated-replay-response.json. The expected filename is only an --arg value; jq's actual input file is unrelated.
findings.impact: The verifier returns PASS even though the request ID was read from an unrelated response. A hand-crafted transcript can still satisfy every Codex objective without correlating the successful replay response to the accepted claim, violating AC-15 and the documented exact response-file input gate.

evidence.description: At the exact head, a temporary negative put replay-response.json in a jq --arg value while the positional input was unrelated-replay-response.json. The assertion failed because verifyClientEvidence resolved PASS with every Codex objective.
The SINGULAR recognizer accepts the expected filename anywhere in the parsed argument list rather than proving it is jq's input operand.
Once that segment is classified as a reader, its request ID output is combined with the replay request path/status and accepted by claim matching.
Cycle 7 covers newline, pipeline, compound-command and multiple-jq boundaries, but not an expected filename used as an option value while another positional file supplies jq input.
The real Codex record passes, and the SHA-bound 206-line Claude transcript prefix also passes. The failure is specifically jq input-operand identity, not positive-evidence availability.
AC-15 requires each named client to actually execute the representative validation, and the plan disallows a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: Parse the supported jq invocation shape and prove the successful replay response file occupies jq's actual input-file operand (or a validated --slurpfile operand), not an arbitrary option value. Add the --arg/positional-input negative while preserving every current segment-boundary, alias, request-ID, status, cross-operation, body/key and live-resource check.
findings.verification: Both current real client records still pass; all existing negatives remain closed; and jq --arg marker replay-response.json '{requestId: .meta.requestId}' unrelated-replay-response.json fails with CLIENT_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED_TRANSCRIPT.

findings.impact: The exact child must be publicly present before COMMITTED/PASS; missing or mismatched children now fail closed.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: The current recovery helper recognizes the bounded retry contract, preserves exact bytes/key and leaves exhaustion OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.

findings.impact: Temporary concurrency no longer becomes terminal local rejection and the original intent remains resumable.

evidence.description: The exact-head regression proves retry-success after two sends and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN after three bounded in-progress responses, with identical body and key.
